hints: Focus on what makes simple molecular substances special, very weak forces between molecules and no free electrons or ions to carry charge.
Look for the combination of low melting point plus no electrical conductivity in any state, that rules out metals and ionic lattices straight away.
Compare the two poor conductors left, one melts near 100 C and one melts above 1500 C, and ask which one fits weak intermolecular forces.
walkthrough:
**Recall the fingerprint of simple molecular**

Think small molecules held together by weak van der Waals forces. That means low melting point, no charges to conduct electricity, and often insoluble in water.

Rule to use: simple molecular = low $mp$ + poor conductor solid, liquid and aqueous.

**Knock out metals and ionic compounds**

Any substance that is a good conductor must have mobile electrons or ions. That is metallic or ionic, never simple molecular.

So A with good conductivity when solid and C with good conductivity must both be ruled out for this question.

**Separate simple molecular from giant molecular**

Both B and D are always poor conductors, so use melting point. B melts at $113 ^{\circ}\text{C}$, easy to separate weak molecules. D melts at $1600 ^{\circ}\text{C}$, which needs very strong covalent bonds throughout a giant lattice to be broken.

Conclusion: only B shows low mp + insoluble + always poor, the classic simple molecular pattern like $\text{S}_8$ or $\text{I}_2$.

options.A: Good conductivity when solid means delocalised electrons, the hallmark of metallic structure. Low mp of 64 C and vigorous reaction with water fits an alkali metal like sodium, not neutral small molecules.
options.B: Low melting point of 113 C shows only weak intermolecular forces are broken on melting. Insoluble in water and always poor conductivity shows no mobile ions or electrons. This is exactly simple molecular.
options.C: High melting point of 767 C plus solubility in water and ability to conduct electricity points to an ionic lattice with strong electrostatic attractions. Mobile ions in molten or aqueous state carry the charge, so it cannot be simple molecular.
options.D: Always poor conductivity might tempt you, but melting point of 1600 C is far too high for weak intermolecular forces. This needs a giant molecular lattice like $\text{SiO}_2$ or diamond where strong covalent bonds run throughout.
